question.problem:
For the functions $f(x)$ and $g(x),$ you are given the following data:

$$
f(4)=2,\,{f}^{′}(4)=\sqrt{2},\,g(4)=\sqrt{2},\,{g}^{′}(4)=-1
$$

Compute $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{f(x)}{g(x)})$ at $x=4.$

${\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{f(x)}{g(x)})|}_{x=4}=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
Using the quotient rule, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{f(x)}{g(x)})=\frac{{f}^{′}(x)g(x)-f(x){g}^{′}(x)}{(g(x))^{2}}.
$$

At the point where $x=4,$ this gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{f(x)}{g(x)})|}_{x=4} & =\frac{{f}^{′}(4)g(4)-f(4){g}^{′}(4)}{(g(4))^{2}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}\cdot \sqrt{2}-2\cdot (-1)}{(\sqrt{2})^{2}} \\  & =\frac{2+2}{2} \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$
